cards.title: STL contract: watertight, consistent normals, mm
cards.when: any STL is about to go into the mesher
cards.statement: Only this STL goes into volume meshing: closed (watertight), with consistent normals (consistent winding), in millimetres, with a passport in stl/registry.csv. A broken STL is fixed first and meshed afterwards; “it built without errors” ≠ “usable”.
recipe: tools/qa/stl_qa.py --stl <file> --expect-volume <mm³> --expect-bodies <n> --json
a PASS verdict is mandatory before snappy/cfMesh; exit 0 pass / 1 fail / 2 input
record units, seed and tessellation tolerances in params.json
evidence: AGENTS.md R9 and §4; registry.csv contains the fields watertight, units, volume_mm3, path

cards.title: STL cleanup is a mandatory step for CAD/CSG output
cards.when: the STL comes from CadQuery/OCC or from boolean operations
cards.statement: A raw OCC STL contains degenerate faces at poles and seams and is almost never watertight. The stl_qa.py --clean-out cleanup rebuilds the surface: vertex merging, removal of degenerate/duplicate faces, winding reconciliation.
recipe: tools/qa/stl_qa.py --stl raw.stl --clean-out clean.stl --json report.json
compare the raw and cleaned metrics: volume/area/bbox must not change beyond tolerance
hand clean.stl to the mesher and keep raw.stl for the protocol
evidence: exp-002/D-007: the raw OCC STL is not watertight, cleanup is mandatory

cards.title: CadQuery tessellation is controlled by angularTolerance, not tolerance
cards.when: CAD geometry is exported to STL and volume/shape matter
cards.statement: Triangulation accuracy is controlled by angularTolerance: 0.1 gives an accurate volume, 0.2–0.3 is coarser and suits meshing (fewer triangles). The tolerance parameter does not affect tessellation.
recipe: accurate volume: angularTolerance 0.1
meshing/large models: angularTolerance 0.2–0.3
after changing angularTolerance, re-measure volume and record it in params.json
evidence: exp-002 and D-017: angularTolerance defines tessellation, tolerance does not

cards.title: Minimum gap ≥ 2·MeshSizeMin
cards.when: pore/channel geometry is being designed for a volume mesh
cards.statement: If the gap between surfaces is smaller than two minimum cells, the mesher physically cannot resolve it: the result is slivers, one-sided interfaces and non-orthogonality around 70–90°. The gap is a geometry parameter, not a mesher setting.
recipe: before generation: gap ≥ 2 × MeshSizeMin
“zero gap” contact between bodies is forbidden — bodies must either intersect or have a gap
if the gap cannot be met, reduce MeshSizeMin and recompute the cell budget
evidence: D-007 and D-008: design rule; exp-002 — a tetra mesh on such an STL is unusable

cards.title: A gmsh tetra mesh is unusable for pore STLs
cards.when: tempted to get a volume mesh quickly from a pore STL via gmsh
cards.statement: On a pore STL a gmsh tetra mesh consistently gives maxNonOrtho 89.37–89.69°; 12 configurations (Algorithm3D 1/4/10, netgen, laplace) did not help. Gmsh tetra is acceptable only as a check “the STL is closed, the volume converges”; for simulations use snappyHexMesh/cfMesh.
recipe: to check closure: gmsh tetra → volume ↔ stl_qa volume
for simulation: snappy (hex-dominant + layers) or cfMesh cartesianMesh
the exception is conformal CHT from OCC geometry (route D), see hint gmsh-route-d
improves: choosing a mesher without wasting time

cards.title: Named patches in the STL save renameBoundary work
cards.when: the boundary has different physical roles (inlet/outlet/walls/interface)
cards.statement: gen_channel_spheres.py with --fluid-patches writes fluid_patches.stl, in which the faces are already split by patch (inlet, outlet, walls, interface, interface_necks). snappy carries the names over through refinementSurfaces patchInfo; cfMesh needs renameBoundary only for unmatched.
recipe: in snappyHexMeshDict list every STL/name in refinementSurfaces with patchInfo { type wall/patch; }
for cfMesh — meshDict renameBoundary.newPatchNames by these names
after meshing check the patch list in checkMesh and the area match against stl_qa --expect-area

cards.title: Sphere packing — two steps with JSON in between
cards.when: a polydisperse/mono sphere packing with necks is needed
cards.statement: First gen_packing_table.py computes the table of balls and contacts (CSV), then gen_packing_stl.py builds the solid and fluid STLs from that table. Skipping the table or hand-editing the CSV breaks reproducibility — the seed and parameters are fixed in params.json.
recipe: step 1: --params-file params.json --out balls.csv --contacts-out contacts.csv
step 2: --balls balls.csv --contacts contacts.csv --solid-out solid.stl --fluid-out fluid.stl
compute large packings on a compute machine (MACHINES.md), not on the laptop
evidence: geometry/packings/gen_packing_table.py and gen_packing_stl.py CLI; exp-010/exp-011 (algorithm and scaled STL)

cards.title: Units: STL in mm, OpenFOAM case in metres
cards.statement: The project's canonical STLs are in mm while the OpenFOAM case is in metres. This is fixed in three places: (1) blockMesh in mm → `convertToMeters 0.001`; (2) geometry{...} in snappyHexMeshDict → scale 0.001 (while the STL is in mm); (3) locationInMesh/locationsInMesh are in metres. The mesh_build scaffold instead writes the case in metres and itself uses the units key probed from the installed build (`scale 1` on the current OpenFOAM.com/.org builds, `convertToMeters 1` on older ones — see mesh_capabilities), while scale 0.001 on geometry stays. A mismatch gives “the point is not inside the mesh” or a mesh 1000 times too large.
recipe: STL: mm (bbox_mm in the stl_qa report)
hand-written blockMeshDict in mm: convertToMeters 0.001
snappy geometry: scale 0.001; locationInMesh in metres
scaffolded case: metres, units key probed by mesh_capabilities (scale on v2512/v2606 and org 14)

cards.title: CadQuery: a compound cut loses the volume of overlapping cavities
cards.when: a block minus several cavities (spheres/cylinders), especially overlapping ones
cards.statement: base.cut(Compound.makeCompound(tools)) subtracts the shared cavity regions twice: the volume comes out below the analytical value. Verified on 2026-11-23 on a 12x6x6 block with two intersecting R=0.8 cylinders: the compound gives 407.872568 mm³, sequential and cut(fuse) give 410.603235 mm³. On 6 cylinders with three overlaps this is 8.192 mm³ = 2.219 % — exactly 3·(16/3)·R³.
recipe: geometry/cad/cq_common.py: cut_tools(..., strategy="sequential") — the default; "fused" is correct too, "single" only for cavities that are known not to intersect
check occ_volume against analytics BEFORE export: gen_cq_porous.py fails (rc=1) when |ΔV_occ| > 0.5 %
for intersecting cylinders V = V_box − Σ πR²h + Σ_overlaps (16/3)R³
the single strategy can be caught via --strategy both: a volume difference > 1e-6 % means intersections
evidence: benchmark 1B (6 cylinders): V=359.647702 vs analytical 367.809705 (−2.219 %), generator.json strategy_used=single
